text:
maya: Quick RFC follow-up — proposing a thin Surface Gateway service that normalizes the public API for Hosted/Dedicated/Private. Link to RFC: https://r.redwood/surface-gw-rfc (draft).

sam: high-level: surface-gw sits in front of runtime endpoints and handles auth mapping, header translation, and routing policies. keeps clients stable while we evolve infra.

liam: concern: added hop -> latency. do we have numbers?

maya: rough numbers from local perf tests: ~0.8ms median p99 ~2.2ms for small JSON pass-through. most overhead is TLS + JSON parsing. we can bypass heavy work for trusted internal flows.

raja: security question — private customers require no control-plane egress. does this gateway break that model?

maya: good catch. design: run surface-gw in two modes: "control-plane-aware" (hosted) and "edge-proxy-only" (private). for private deployments surface-gw can be deployed inside customer VPC w/ no external control-plane calls. config translation happens from local control plane.

sam: how does it handle model variants fallbacks? currently runtime routing logic lives in control plane.

liam: idea: gateway should carry a routing-policy token (signed) that the runtime can trust. gateway validates client auth, asks control-plane for policy when needed, caches signed policy for X seconds, forwards token to runtime. runtime validates signature and skips control-plane lookup.

maya: example header mapping we discussed:

```
# incoming request
Authorization: Bearer user-key
X-Requested-Model: redwood/llama-2-7b
X-Tenant-ID: t-123

# gateway -> runtime
X-Routing-Policy: sig:v1:eyJ...
X-Tenant: t-123
X-Original-Auth: redacted
```

raja: caching signed policy is fine but we need revocation support. if a tenant changes rollout we must force refresh.

maya: we'll ship a revocation endpoint and short TTLs by default (30s) and offer longer TTL on dedicated where we want predictability. revocation can be pushed via control-plane pubsub.

devex-jen: from SDK/compatibility POV we want zero changes for customers. they keep sending the same public API. good. also need to document rate-limit behavior differences between hosted and dedicated.

sam: observability — add tags: surface.instance_id, deployment_mode(hosted|dedicated|private), routing_policy_id, tenant_id. propagate trace id.

liam: telemetry plan also needs token-level token spending attribution — gateway must attribute tokens before batching when possible. tricky for batching across tenants.

maya: plan: gateway exposes two modes for batching: isolated-per-tenant and multi-tenant pooled. default for hosted = pooled (cost efficient). dedicated/private default = isolated. config via tenant profile.

raja: what about replay/response signing for customer audit? some regulated customers want tamper-proof logs.

maya: gateway can compute HMAC of request/response and store headers pointing to audit-log blob in s3 or local archive for private. add option per-customer.

liam: rollout strategy?

maya: stage 1: internal-only prototype behind feature flag (eng infra). stage 2: opt-in for low-risk hosted tenants + Dedicated pilot. stage 3: default for new tenants, opt-out for existing. private always opt-in.

sam: canary rules: route X% of traffic by header, verify latency, error, quality regressions using Redwood Optimize eval hooks. if metrics cross threshold -> rollback.

devex-jen: docs checklist: API compatibility, headers, SDK changes (none), rate-limit semantics, troubleshooting, how to opt-in/opt-out.

raja: ops checklist: revocation flow tested, KMS integration for signing, RBAC for control-plane access, network placement docs for private mode.

liam: one more tradeoff — single gateway simplifies client surface but centralizes policy. makes cascade failure possible. do we need per-region active-active gateways?

maya: yes, design requires regional gateways with leaderless control-plane cache. fallback rules: if regional gateway loses control-plane connectivity, it should switch to cached mode w/ stricter quotas and circuit-breaker.

deploy-bot: maya requested deployment of feature-branch surface-gw/prototype to infra-dev at 2024-11-05T18:02:00Z — status: queued.

sam: next steps: I'll draft a short RFC appendix with APIs and header contract. liam will prototype signed-policy flow. raja will outline security gating. devex-jen will stub docs.

maya: thanks everyone. small ask: keep messages in thread with any blockers. aim to review appendix by EOW. :thumbsup:
